children: AMMAN — Jordan aims to boost local manufacturers’ participation in major national projects worth JD8.9 billion, including opportunities linked to the Amra City development, under its Engineering Industries Sector Strategy for 2026–2029.

Developed by the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply in cooperation with the Jordan Chamber of Industry (JCI) and other stakeholders, the strategy seeks to expand domestic production and strengthen local supply chains by helping Jordanian manufacturers compete for procurement contracts.

It identifies major infrastructure and development projects as potential sources of demand for engineering products, provided local manufacturers meet technical specifications, quality standards and supply requirements.

The strategy includes a programme to increase local content in major national projects, strengthen cooperation between manufacturers and contractors, and retain a greater share of project spending within the Jordanian economy.

According to the strategy, the engineering industries sector comprises around 4,800 establishments employing 35,200 people. It generated JD620 million in added value in 2024, with total production approaching JD2 billion.

Proposed initiatives include establishing an engineering innovation complex in Zarqa, incorporating a metal-forming technology centre and an engineering training centre, and setting up a joint industrial research and development fund.
The strategy also seeks to diversify export markets by capitalising on free trade agreements and Jordan’s proximity to regional markets.
Jordanian engineering exports to Syria rose by 282 per cent in 2025 to around JD37 million, up from JD9.7 million before Syria’s political transition in December 2024, according to the strategy.
